articles.title: Scuffle at Education Directorate: Director Injured After Clash with BJP MLA, Staff Threaten Strike
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: There was chaos at the Directorate of Elementary Education in Dehradun on Saturday after a confrontation between BJP MLA Umesh Sharma Kau and officials turned violent. Director Ajay Kumar Nautiyal sustained a serious head injury and was rushed to Coronation Hospital for treatment.

body.html:
There was chaos at the Directorate of Elementary Education in Dehradun on Saturday after a confrontation between BJP MLA Umesh Sharma Kau and officials turned violent. Director Ajay Kumar Nautiyal sustained a serious head injury and was rushed to Coronation Hospital for treatment. Doctors later said his condition is stable.

What Triggered the Dispute?
According to officials, the controversy relates to a name change on a stone plaque installed at a Government Primary School campus in the Raipur block. The matter had reportedly been referred to the government for a decision at the Secretary level. Officials said no formal order had been issued so far.

The MLA had earlier written to authorities regarding the issue. On Saturday (21 Feb 2026) around 11:30 am, he allegedly arrived at the director’s office with over two dozen supporters to discuss the matter.

Scuffle Inside Office:
Eyewitnesses said the discussion escalated into a heated argument. A scuffle broke out between departmental employees and the MLA’s supporters. During the chaos, Director Nautiyal was allegedly struck near his eye, suffering a serious injury. There are also allegations that chairs were thrown and office property was damaged.

Conflicting Claims:
Both sides have made counter-allegations.

Director Nautiyal claimed the MLA and his supporters entered aggressively, abused him and attempted to force their way inside by locking the door.

The MLA’s side alleged they were attacked by staff and that the gate was locked from outside during the altercation.

Confusion remains over who locked the room during the incident.

Staff Outrage, Demand Action:
The episode has triggered anger among Education Department employees, who say disagreements could have been resolved administratively rather than through confrontation. Employee unions have demanded that an FIR be registered against those responsible and have warned of a strike if strict action is not taken.

The incident has also raised concerns over security arrangements at government offices in the state capital. Further legal action is awaited.

articles.title: Viral Video from Malviya Nagar Sparks Fresh Debate on Racial Harassment
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A viral video from Malviya Nagar has brought attention to alleged racial harassment following a minor residential dispute. According to available information, the incident occurred on February 19 during AC repair work in a fourth-floor flat.

body.html:
A viral video from Malviya Nagar has brought attention to alleged racial harassment following a minor residential dispute.

According to available information, the incident occurred on February 19 during AC repair work in a fourth-floor flat. Dust generated from drilling reportedly led to an argument with residents living on the lower floor. Three women from Arunachal Pradesh alleged that the confrontation escalated into verbal abuse and racial remarks targeting people from the Northeast.

Police were called to the spot and formal procedures were reportedly carried out. The women have demanded a formal apology, stating that the alleged remarks were not only directed at them personally but were offensive to the wider Northeastern community.

The episode has once again raised concerns about racial discrimination faced by individuals from Northeast India in metropolitan cities. The women said the issue could have been resolved through communication rather than escalation.

Authorities have not yet issued a detailed public statement on further action.

articles.title: 4-Hour High Alert in Haridwar: Abducted Toddler Found Abandoned Near Rishikul Chowk
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A quiet night in Haridwar turned tense after a two-year-old girl was allegedly abducted from a family sleeping on the footpath in the Tulsi Chowk area. The incident reportedly took place between 1 am and 2 am.

body.html:
A quiet night in Haridwar turned tense after a two-year-old girl was allegedly abducted from a family sleeping on the footpath in the Tulsi Chowk area.

The incident reportedly took place between 1 am and 2 am. According to eyewitnesses, the family was asleep on the sidewalk when an unidentified man allegedly took advantage of the darkness and abducted the child. The mother discovered the girl missing after waking up, triggering panic and a frantic search. When the family failed to trace her, police were informed.

Massive Police Response

Following the alert, Senior Superintendent of Police Navneet Singh took charge and mobilised multiple teams, including the local police station, Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) and CIU. Checking operations were launched across key junctions and exit routes in the city.

Search operations extended from Tulsi Chowk to the railway station, bus stand and highway areas. Police scanned footage from hundreds of CCTV cameras and deployed drones and mobile surveillance units to track suspicious movement.

Child Found After 4 Hours

After nearly four hours of high alert, the accused allegedly abandoned the girl near Rishikul Chowk and fled under the cover of darkness. Around 5 am, police received information about a child found crying alone. The team reached the spot, confirmed her identity and safely reunited her with her family.

The girl is reported to be safe. A medical examination was conducted as a precaution.

Investigation Underway

While the family expressed relief, the incident has raised serious security concerns. Police are analysing CCTV footage and questioning local residents and those living nearby to identify the suspect. Authorities are probing whether the act was linked to human trafficking or committed by an individual acting alone.

SSP Navneet Singh said a special team has been formed to trace the accused and urged residents not to spread rumours but to report any suspicious activity immediately.

The incident has sparked debate over the safety of families living on footpaths and the need for strengthened night shelter facilities and surveillance in the city.

articles.title: Mining Mafia Attacks Forest Team in CM Dhami’s Home District, Attempt to Run Over Officer Alleged
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A forest department team was allegedly attacked by members of the mining mafia while attempting to stop illegal mining in the Ransali Range of Sitarganj in Udham Singh Nagar district, Uttarakhand.

body.html:
A forest department team was allegedly attacked by members of the mining mafia while attempting to stop illegal mining in the Ransali Range of Sitarganj in Udham Singh Nagar district, Uttarakhand.

The incident occurred near the Kailash River area, where a forest patrol team spotted three tractor-trailers being loaded with illegally mined minerals. When officials sought documents from those present at the site, the accused allegedly turned violent.

According to reports, three personnel, including Forest Inspector Nand Kishore Pandey, were assaulted. It is also alleged that the attackers attempted to run over a forest officer with a tractor during the confrontation.

Based on a complaint filed by the forest ranger, police have registered a case against three accused, including a father-son duo, and launched an investigation.

The incident has drawn attention as it took place in Udham Singh Nagar, the home district of Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami. A video purportedly showing the clash between officials and the alleged mining mafia has gone viral on social media.

Legal proceedings are underway, and further action is expected based on the outcome of the investigation.

articles.title: 5 Years After Surgery, Scissors Found Inside Woman’s Abdomen in Kerala
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a shocking case of alleged medical negligence, a surgical scissor was found inside the abdomen of a 51-year-old woman nearly five years after she underwent a hysterectomy at Government Medical College Hospital Alappuzha.

body.html:
In a shocking case of alleged medical negligence, a surgical scissor was found inside the abdomen of a 51-year-old woman nearly five years after she underwent a hysterectomy at Government Medical College Hospital Alappuzha.

The scissors, identified as a long, curved Metzenbaum instrument used during surgeries, were detected in Usha Josephkutty, a resident of Punnapra, after she complained of persistent abdominal pain and blood in her urine.

The hysterectomy was performed on May 10, 2021. Since then, Usha had been seeking treatment at various hospitals for recurring pain, but the cause remained undiagnosed. On Wednesday, an X-ray taken on the advice of a urology specialist revealed the presence of the surgical instrument.

She visited the medical college hospital at Vandanam on Thursday morning. According to a relative, some doctors allegedly asked the family not to disclose the matter.

Usha, a daily wage worker under the employment guarantee scheme, lives in a rented house in Paravur with her husband Josephkutty, a labourer. Following the discovery, she expressed fear about returning to the Alappuzha medical college and said she preferred to undergo further surgery elsewhere.

She was later shifted to Amrita Hospital in Kochi late at night, accompanied by her son Shibin.

Punnapra South grama panchayat vice-president KF Tobias demanded emergency financial assistance for the family. Meanwhile, hospital superintendent Dr A. Harikumar stated that an inquiry would be conducted and that no formal complaint had been received so far.

The Director of Medical Education has also ordered a probe into the incident.

articles.title: PSI Booked for Alleged Assault on Youth Who Reported After Securing Bail
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A Police Sub-Inspector has been booked for allegedly assaulting a youth who had obtained anticipatory bail and reported to the Magadi Road Police Station as required.

body.html:
A Police Sub-Inspector has been booked for allegedly assaulting a youth who had obtained anticipatory bail and reported to the Magadi Road Police Station as required.

According to the complaint, PSI Kaushik allegedly abused and assaulted Avinash when he appeared at the station in connection with a cheating case linked to a chit fund. Avinash had secured anticipatory bail and was complying with the condition to report before the police.

The complaint states that Kaushik allegedly questioned him, saying, “You’ve come with bail?” and physically assaulted him in front of his sister. He also allegedly threatened to implicate him in another case and have him declared a “rowdy” if he secured bail in the present matter.

A medical report reportedly notes soft tissue damage to Avinash’s left ear.

After approaching a court, Avinash filed a formal complaint, following which an FIR was registered at the Magadi Road Police Station. The complaint further alleges that the PSI assaulted Avinash’s mother and sister and that they were detained without prior notice.

Police have registered a case against Kaushik, Lakshmi and Narasimha, and initiated an investigation. Avinash has claimed that the alleged assault was retaliatory in nature for reporting to the station after obtaining bail.

articles.title: Caught Cheating, Student Assaults Professor in Kalaburagi College
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking incident of violence against a faculty member has been reported from a homeopathy college in Kalaburagi, Karnataka, on 18 Feb 2026, where a student allegedly assaulted an assistant professor after being caught cheating during an internal examination.

body.html:
A shocking incident of violence against a faculty member has been reported from a homeopathy college in Kalaburagi, Karnataka, on 18 Feb 2026, where a student allegedly assaulted an assistant professor after being caught cheating during an internal examination.

According to sources, the incident occurred inside the examination hall when the student, identified as Shahbaz, was allegedly found using a mobile phone to copy answers. The block supervisor, Assistant Professor Shivarajkumar, reportedly questioned the student, confiscated his answer script and directed him to leave the hall immediately.

Enraged over the disciplinary action, the student allegedly turned violent and physically assaulted the professor in full view of faculty members and students, creating panic on the campus.

The college administration has taken a strict stand on the matter. The student’s parents have been informed, and he has been officially debarred from appearing in future examinations.

Further action, if any, is expected as per institutional and legal procedures.

articles.title: Stones Hurled During Shivaji Jayanti Rally in Bagalkote, Section 163 Imposed
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Tension prevailed briefly in Bagalkote, Karnataka, after stones were allegedly hurled at a Shivaji Jayanti procession in the old city area on Thursday, officials said. The incident occurred when the rally, which began around 3:30 pm, was passing near a mosque.

body.html:
Tension prevailed briefly in Bagalkote, Karnataka, after stones were allegedly hurled at a Shivaji Jayanti procession in the old city area on Thursday, officials said.

The incident occurred when the rally, which began around 3:30 pm, was passing near a mosque. According to Superintendent of Police Siddharth Goyal, adequate police force had been deployed for the procession and senior officers were present at the spot.

“As the procession approached the mosque area, two stones were thrown from a distance towards us,” the SP said. Based on preliminary information and video footage reviewed so far, one stone hit a police constable, while the other struck him on the shoulder. No major injuries were reported.

Despite the incident, the procession continued without further disruption and the situation remained peaceful, police said.

Authorities have reviewed CCTV footage from the area, which is under camera surveillance. The procession was also recorded. Police said strict action will be taken against those involved.

Meanwhile, prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita have been imposed in parts of Bagalkote from midnight of February 19 to midnight of February 24. Under the restrictions, assembly of more than four persons in public places is banned. Carrying weapons, organising meetings or sit-ins without prior permission, and activities endangering public safety have also been prohibited.

Police said the situation is under control and adequate security arrangements are in place to maintain law and order.
